title: Integer `sum`
verdict: deviation: unbounded, and reported as a warning
description: Shim. `SUM(BIGINT)` returns `HUGEINT` and never overflows at 64 bits, so DuckDB alone answers where the reference raises. `CAST(SUM(x) AS BIGINT)` raises past `i64`. sverify's written plan already guards this and raises (`test_sum.test:68`).

`avg` of integers returns `DOUBLE` in DuckDB (duckdb-avg-int). sverify's written SQL computes an `i64` average as the exact `HUGEINT` sum `//` the count (`int_avg` in `python/src/sverify/sql/duckdb.py`). DataFusion's `avg` is a double, so it refuses an integer one.
reference: Substrait and the reference: `sum` of `i8`…`i64` returns `i64?`; with `overflow` omitted, a sum outside `i64` raises.

Lean: deviation. The sum is unbounded, and `verify` reports it as a warning (`may wrap around`, `sumWraps`); the parser accepts only `SILENT`. `SUM(b)` of values summing past `2⁶³` answers `4611686018427388403500`, and `SUM(b)::BIGINT` the same, since a cast to `BIGINT` is not checked.

`avg` of integers (decided on #209, fixed): it follows the plan's declared output type. With `fp64` (DataFusion's plans), it is the mean as a double; with `i64` (Substrait's own impl), it is the exact mean truncated toward zero (`AggFn.iavg`), which always fits.

provenance.notes: `avg` of integers follows the declared output type.

provenance.checked_by: characterization pipeline round 2 (source; aggregates, windows, relations, temporal, nested, strings)

evidence.note: GetSumAggregate: SMALLINT, INTEGER, BIGINT, HUGEINT overloads, each returning HUGEINT
IntegerSumOperation (SMALLINT): int64 state, finalized to HUGEINT
SumPropagateStats: swaps in sum_no_overflow (int64 state) when the statistics bound the sum within int64; the result stays HUGEINT
Hugeint::Add (merging states) raises OutOfRange past 128 bits
TINYINT binds the BIGINT overload: implicit cast cost 101 against 110 for SMALLINT

provenance.notes: Read at tag v2.0.0 (commit d54cbbe3). `sum` of `TINYINT` (through the `BIGINT` overload), `SMALLINT` and `INTEGER` returns `HUGEINT`, like `BIGINT`; each width is its own template instantiation. `SMALLINT` accumulates in an unchecked `int64_t`, out of reach below 2^48 rows; `INTEGER` and `BIGINT` in an exact `HUGEINT`, whose merge raises only past 128 bits. So no sum of `i8` to `i32` overflows or raises at 64 bits, as for `i64`.
